issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md R042 item 2 (commit 75dc46a6; decision record beadrs-691c4fec). Operator-requested 2026-10-28. Evidence comes from a 2026-10-28 sweep of 98 bead-rs workspaces on codinghome (50,819 beads, copies deduplicated) and of transcripts from 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-28 (292,734 bead-related shell commands; regex baselines, not release claims).

Clean-room rule: amend the governing file under research/specs/ first, in its own commit, then implement only from it.

## Evidence
- `bead claim <id>` was attempted 196 times in 171 sessions; 114 attempts failed with "unexpected argument".
- `bead why <id>` failed 53 times, because `why` requires `--id`.
- ~/CLAUDE.md documents `bead claim <id>`.
- Today's workaround is `update --status in_progress --assignee`, which skips the frontier checks.

## Scope
- Spec: amend research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md and research/specs/agent-ergonomics-v1.md to define `bead claim [ID]`.
- **With ID:** in one IMMEDIATE transaction, claim ID only if it is in the ready frontier under exactly the frontier-claim rules: open, unassigned, unblocked, and not excluded by policy or resource locks. Return the same claim epoch, lease, credential output and JSON shape as a frontier claim.
- **Refusal:** otherwise exit 4 with no mutation and a stable reason code in text and JSON: `not_open`, `assigned`, `blocked` (naming the blockers), `excluded` (naming the rule). An unknown ID exits 3.
- **Without ID:** behavior is unchanged.
- **Positional ID:** every subcommand that takes a single issue through `--id` (today `why`, `data get|set|list|remove` and `ref`; enumerate from help) also accepts it positionally.
  - `--id` keeps working.
  - Both forms with different values is a usage error, exit 2, naming the conflict.
- `capabilities` advertises `targeted_claim: true` and `positional_id: true`.

## Ordering
Blocked by beadrs-ab4a2b91, because the claimant-credential fence rewrites the same claim paths.

## Acceptance
- Separate-process concurrency tests:
  - two racing `claim X` calls give exactly one success;
  - `claim X` racing a frontier `claim` never double-claims.
- Each refusal reason has a test.
- Frontier `claim` output is byte-identical to before.
- A test enumerates every subcommand with an `--id` option and asserts that the positional form works.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass on the pushed commit.
issue.title: Claim a named ready issue with `claim ID`, and accept a positional ID wherever --id is taken (R042.2)

issue.description:
Field evidence gathered 2026-10-23 on codinghome: a sweep of all 92 bead-rs workspaces under /home/coding, git object accounting in the largest repos, and every bead invocation in agent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects (32,149 calls) and ~/.codex/sessions (80,311 calls). Counts are regex-based and approximate.

Measured over the last 30 days (uncompressed blob bytes added to git history under .beads):
- tradegraph-platform (sharded mode, 1,206 beads): 2,400 checkpoint commits, 13.8 GB, 5.7 MB per commit; pack is now 826 MiB.
- bead-rs (monolithic, 891 beads): 1,391 commits, 4.05 GB, 2.9 MB per commit; 98% of all blob bytes committed in the period.
- ARMOR (monolithic, 2,981 beads): 105 commits, 2.5 GB, 24 MB per commit.
- NEEDLE (monolithic, 3,298 beads): 64 commits, 2.4 GB, 37 MB per commit.
- commitgraph (sharded, 3,080 beads): 4 commits, 110 MB, 27.6 MB per commit.
Bytes scale with store size, not with what changed, in both modes. Delta compression hides some of it in the pack, but every clone, fetch and push still pays, and Forgejo has refused oversized pushes before.

Spec-first child: the implementation child (field-evidence-2026-10-23:incremental-impl) is blocked on this one. The normative checkpoint spec must exist before implementation evidence is accepted (plan section 13).

Decisions this spec records (settled; the spec defines them precisely):
- Issue state lives in many small content-addressed issue shards, partitioned by issue-ID prefix and sized so a typical shard stays under 64 KiB. A one-issue mutation rewrites only the shard holding that issue.
- Events live in sealed, immutable, append-only segments plus one open tail segment. A mutation appends to the tail; a segment seals at a size bound and is never rewritten.
- Pointer and manifest files stay small: their size grows with the number of shards, never with issue or event content.
- `forensic.jsonl` is not rewritten on each publication in this layout.
- Adaptive mode selects this layout for every workspace. Monolithic remains only as an explicit forced mode, with its existing safety limits.
- Migration: the first publication under the new layout is a full rewrite and is documented as such; restore, reconcile, fork and verified-restore read both layouts.
- Budget: a single-issue update in a 3,000-issue workspace adds at most 256 KiB of new blob bytes per publication, pointer files included.

Also state in the spec that the ten pending, unapproved proposals asking to make sharded mode reachable (beadrs-292dfbbe, 36340b5e, 37da66c7, 62acb271, 84f9a125, 9269c2fd, c2b0b216, d23fdce6, e5c770dc, f4b70090) rest on a stale premise: sharded mode is live in 3 workspaces and does not bound bytes. Leave their disposition to the human reviewer.

Clean-room: author all prose independently from public format facts and our own measurements.

Acceptance:
- research/specs/checkpoint-set-v1.md (or a v2 successor it names) defines the layout, partitioning, sealing, migration and the byte budget, with named conformance scenarios.
- docs/plan/plan.md records the requirement with the measurements above.
- Committed and pushed.
